#Part 1
1.Open the sleep dataset in R
```{r}
data(sleep)
```

2. Is it long or wide format? How do you know?
```{r}
##Long format, this is because the dataset has multiple rows for each group instead of their own column (hence the "long" format of the data"),
```

3. Transform this data so that it is in the other format.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
wideSleep <- pivot_wider(sleep, id_cols= "ID", names_from= "group", values_from = "extra", names_prefix = "group")
```

4. Transform your data back to its original format
```{r}
longSleep <- pivot_longer(wideSleep, cols= c(group1, group2), names_to="group", values_to="extra")
```

5. Open the Starwars dataset
```{r}
data(starwars)
```

6. Create homeworld as a factor. How many levels does it have?
```{r}
starwars$homeworld <- as.factor(starwars$homeworld)
nlevels(starwars$homeworld)
```

7. Reorder homeworld so that Naboo is the reference group
```{r}
starwars$homeworld <- relevel(starwars$homeworld, ref= "Naboo")
levels(starwars$homeworld)
```

8. Use mutate to create a column transforming kg to pounds. (hint: you may need to look up the conversion)
```{r}
library(dplyr)
newWeight <-starwars |> mutate(massP= mass*2.20462) |> select(mass, massP)

```

9. Print a summary of your column from #8
```{r}
summary(newWeight$massP)
```


#Part 2
10. open the billboard dataset.
```{r}
data(billboard)
```

11. are the data in this dataframe in long or wide format? explain how you know.
```{r}
##The data is wide format, as each seperate week has its own column (76 week columns). 
```

12. change the data from its original format to the other version.
```{r}
longBillboard<- pivot_longer(billboard, cols= c(colnames(billboard)[4:79]), names_to= "weeks", values_to="position", values_drop_na = TRUE)
```

13. change it from your altered version in #3 back to its original state.
```{r}
wideBillboard<- pivot_wider(longBillboard, id_cols= c("track", "artist", "date.entered"), names_from = "weeks", values_from= "position")
```

14. Separate the date entered column into three columns: one for year, one for month, and one for day.
```{r}
library(tidyr)
wideBillboard <- wideBillboard |> separate(date.entered, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-")
```
